answer.generated: Pooling achieves invariance to translation by reducing the spatial dimensions of the input while retaining important features, thus making the feature representations less sensitive to small shifts in the input image. This is accomplished through operations such as max-pooling, which selects the maximum value within a local neighborhood, effectively downscaling the image and discarding less significant details. In contrast, directly translating the input image would move the entire image, potentially altering the relative positions of features, thereby changing the feature representations more significantly.
